investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Cluster Nodes
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected as Unschedulable: the 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the pod never left the pending state, so the eval runner could not reach the agent creation or VM readiness steps required by the expected-output contract.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes scheduler could not place the remote agent pod on any of the 6 available nodes: the 2 nodes that carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource had no remaining capacity (Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm), and the other 4 nodes were excluded by the pod's node affinity/selector. Preemption was also unavailable on both node groups. Because the pod remained unscheduled for ~126–146 seconds across all three checks, the eval runner never obtained a VM ID or a running/idle/ready remote state, causing a total contract gap for all four required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState).

possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the 2 eligible nodes: all available VM slots are consumed by existing remote agent pods or other workloads, leaving no capacity for new probe pods.

Secondary — node affinity/selector misconfiguration or drift: the 4 non-kata nodes do not match the pod's required node selector, which may reflect a correct constraint (kata peer-pods only run on specific nodes) or a stale/incorrect selector that is excluding nodes that could otherwise serve the workload.

Quaternary — leaked or un-cleaned remote agent pods from prior eval runs consuming VM slots: the withCleanup wrapper in run-status-probes.mjs (line 1883) is responsible for teardown; if cleanup failed in a previous run, slots may remain occupied.

investigation.title: Remote Agents: All Three Checks Failing — Kubernetes kata.peerpods.io/vm Resource Exhaustion Blocking Pod Scheduling
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api on 2026-06-28 with identical Kubernetes scheduling errors: the cluster's 6 nodes cannot schedule new kata peer-pod VMs because 2 nodes report insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and the remaining 4 nodes do not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Because no pod was ever scheduled, the eval runner's createAgent call never returned an agent, and the remote-agent-state check produced zero evidence — all four required fields (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) are missing.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature has exhausted its schedulable kata.peerpods.io/vm resource slots across all eligible nodes. At the time of the eval run, 0 of 6 nodes could accept a new kata peer-pod: 2 nodes had insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm quota and 4 nodes did not satisfy the pod's node affinity/selector constraints. Preemption was also unavailable (no preemption victims found on the 2 eligible nodes). Because the eval runner calls createAgent to provision a remote agent pod before it can poll state, the pod remained unscheduled for ~145 s and the check timed out before any agent identity or state was returned. This is an eval-observed infrastructure scheduling failure localized to the remote-agents Kubernetes node pool; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Cluster Nodes
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected as Unschedulable: the 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the pod never left the pending state, so the eval runner could not reach the agent creation or VM readiness steps required by the expected-output contract.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes scheduler could not place the remote agent pod on any of the 6 available nodes: the 2 nodes that carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource had no remaining capacity (Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm), and the other 4 nodes were excluded by the pod's node affinity/selector. Preemption was also unavailable on both node groups. Because the pod remained unscheduled for ~126–146 seconds across all three checks, the eval runner never obtained a VM ID or a running/idle/ready remote state, causing a total contract gap for all four required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState).

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pods Unschedulable Due to Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity — All Three Remote-Agent Checks Failing
investigations.summary: All three remote-agent eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api on 2026-06-28 with identical Kubernetes scheduling errors: the cluster's 6 nodes have only 2 nodes eligible for kata peer-pod VMs, and both of those nodes report Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity. Because no pod could be scheduled, the agent VM was never provisioned, and the runtime eval never produced any evidence — all 5 required fields (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) are missing from the check result.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the production-api remote-agent swarm has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the 2 nodes that match the remote-agent pod affinity/selector. The remaining 4 nodes do not satisfy the pod's node affinity or selector constraints and are therefore ineligible. With zero schedulable nodes and no preemption victims available, every remote-agent pod request times out unscheduled (~126–152 s), preventing agent creation, state polling, and runtime execution entirely. This is an infrastructure-layer capacity constraint, not an application code defect. No user-traffic or incident signals are present in the evidence; the impact is scoped to these observability evals.

possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the 2 eligible nodes: all available VM slots are occupied by existing workloads, leaving no capacity for new eval pods. This is directly stated in the scheduler message (evidence: failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-create, sibling.remote-agent-state).

Secondary — node affinity/selector misconfiguration or drift: 4 of 6 nodes do not match the pod's affinity/selector, reducing the schedulable pool to only 2 nodes. If this ratio has changed (e.g., nodes were drained, relabeled, or replaced), effective capacity would have dropped without any code change.

Tertiary — cluster under-provisioning for concurrent eval runs: if multiple eval runs or production workloads compete for the same kata.peerpods.io/vm slots simultaneously, transient exhaustion could occur even if steady-state capacity is sufficient.

Lower probability — node affinity/selector on the remote-agent pod spec is overly restrictive and excludes nodes that could otherwise host kata peer-pods, artificially shrinking the eligible pool to 2 nodes.
